themes.name: Steel
pros: Same structure and mood as today, so nothing has to be relearned; the safe default
Every text token now passes 4.5:1 on every row state, including TextFaint and red on selected rows
Friendly (light teal) and Enemy (deeper red) now differ in lightness as well as hue
Panel2 is a lighter step above Panel, so stat cards, grid headers and checked chips are visible
Calmer blue accent and slightly larger radii reduce the harshness of the current look
cons: Least distinctive of the three; reads as a generic dark dashboard
The text ramp is compressed: TextDim and TextFaint are closer together than before
Teal vs red still relies partly on hue for red-green colour-blind users (lightness helps, not solves)
Panel2 lighter than Panel inverts today's inset look; views that used it as a recess look raised

themes.name: Chart Room
pros: The only light theme, and clearly different: paper, navy ink and brass read as a logbook
Highest text contrast of the three (Text on Panel about 15:1); easy to read in a bright room
Hairline borders and small radii give a calm, printed-table look to the team lists
Serif headings (Georgia) set it apart without any bundled font
cons: Bright surface next to a dark game is tiring when alt-tabbing at night
Rating and class colours must be dark to pass on paper, so they look muted and closer together
Brass accent cannot double as the blue rating band; the mock-up uses ClassDD blue for PR 1750-2099
Georgia has old-style figures and Cambria numbers are less even than Segoe UI in dense columns
Canvas views with hard-coded dark colours (replay map, armour viewer) will look pasted in

themes.name: Combat Information Center
pros: Highest contrast of the dark themes (Text on Panel about 17:1); built for a glance mid-battle
Blue vs orange team colours are safe for red-green colour blindness and differ strongly in lightness
24 px rows and monospaced numbers fit more players and make columns line up exactly
Sharp corners and condensed Bahnschrift headers give a distinct instrument-panel character
cons: Dense and stark; tiring for long sessions in Analytics or Ship Intelligence
Condensed headers need FontStretch support in the styles, not just a family name
Orange Enemy sits close to StatusAmber and the BB class colour, so amber carries three meanings
Cyan accent plus saturated rating colours can feel loud on screens with many coloured numbers
Square corners only hold if the remaining hard-coded radii (status pill 13, nav highlight 6, team-table top edge) become tokens too
